jobs.title: Hazardous Materials & Environmental Evaluations
jobs.description:
Final Filing Date:
9/1/2026

As a matrixed multi-disciplinary environmental team, the Environmental Services Branch provides comprehensive and specialized environmental regulatory compliance services to support the Department's wide range of activities. Under the general direction of the Manager in the CEQA and NEPA Support Section, the incumbent supervises and directs the work activities of the Hazardous Materials and Environmental Evaluations Unit (HAZMATEE). HAZMATEE provides comprehensive environmental site assessment, document preparation, permitting, surveying, monitoring, environmental sampling and analysis, and consultant oversight services to ensure DWR's compliance with applicable federal, State, and local environmental laws and regulations in support of DWR's continued operation and maintenance of the State Water Project; flood risk reduction activities; and restoration of the State's ecosystem. This position works collaboratively and in close coordination with the Environmental Assessments and Permitting Section, which ensures multi-disciplinary support amongst the Branch, Division, and Department-wide, and with federal, State, and local agencies and interested parties.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Final Filing Date:
9/3/2026

The Department of Water Resources' (DWR) Northern Region Office is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Environmental Scientist
to join our collaborative team of professionals dedicated to protecting and managing California's water resources. If you enjoy meaningful, hands-on work, thrive in a dynamic environment, and are passionate about making a positive impact on Northern California's communities and natural resources, we encourage you to apply.

In this role, you will perform complex environmental research, field investigations, surveys, and technical analyses, with an emphasis on botanical surveys, that support critical water resource management and restoration projects.

Responsibilities include conducting sensitive plant species surveys, aquatic resources delineations, and vegetation classification and mapping; preparing technical and environmental documentation; conducting recreation surveys, managing grant-funded projects; and collaborating throughout the Northern Region with other DWR offices on a variety of environmental initiatives. This is an excellent opportunity to work alongside a multidisciplinary team, gain diverse field and project experience, and contribute to projects that help protect California's water, native plants, sensitive vegetation communities, recreation resources, and the environment for future generations.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.
